causes.reason: Initial iOS source applies listening.canvas to a VStack without an explicit containing accessibility element (lines 165–168). Original ready native snapshots in both independent input routes expose eleven descendants as listening.canvas and none of the required stable child IDs; source declarations alone are not the proof. Both panels independently confirm A-identifiers. Final anonymous sources add .accessibilityElement(children: .contain); both original final native trees expose one canvas plus distinct title, text, switch, action and option IDs, and their approved route dispatches succeed. This matches one iOS canvas identity cause across states and routes. Separate from option-native-semantics: canvas containment and option wrapping are different modifier sites and satisfy different native propositions; fixing either alone does not logically establish the other.

causes.reason: Initial iOS option source inserts .accessibilityElement(children: .ignore) outside each native Button before its label/selected trait/identifier modifiers (lines 207–212). In both original ready native trees the outer role-1 wrapper has title + em dash + detail, while the unnamed role-9 button child has the automatic comma label. Both panels independently confirm O-semantics. Final sources remove that synthetic ignored-children element, and both final native trees expose exactly the required ID and em-dash label directly on role-9 option buttons with observed native dispatch. This is one iOS option semantic composition cause across all options/states/routes, requiring an option-specific correction independent of the root canvas containment correction. It establishes accessibility/testability, not an unexecuted business/callback defect.
